title: Flatness and an adically formally smooth closed fibre imply adic formal smoothness
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$, with maximal ideal $\overline{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and its induced $k$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $f$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\overline B$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\overline{\mathfrak m}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Then $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NQ, proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs, implication (2) => (3). The fibre B tensor_A k is its canonical quotient B/m_A B. Definition 07NI is the equivalent condition (2)(b) of Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth), namely the discrete-base definition used in def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic.

proof.text: *Reduction to complete local rings.* Put $A^\wedge=\varprojlim A/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion], $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is flat; by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] these are Noetherian complete local rings with the original residue fields. The closed fibre $B^\wedge/\mathfrak m_A B^\wedge$ is the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic completion of $\overline B$: quotienting $B^\wedge$ by $\mathfrak m_A B^\wedge$ gives the inverse limit of $B/(\mathfrak m_AB+\mathfrak m_B^n)$, which is $\varprojlim\overline B/\mathfrak m_{\overline B}^n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] and the Noetherian quotient identification [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient]. Hence this fibre is formally smooth over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion] applied to the hypothesis on $\overline B$. We prove the result first for the complete map $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs), proof of (2) => (3), opening completion reduction; Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), Algebra Lemma Tag 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat)

proof.text: *Cohen presentation.* For the complete map, use [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-cohen-presentation] (Stacks 07NN): there is a commutative square $R\xrightarrow{u}S$, $R\twoheadrightarrow A^\wedge$, $S\twoheadrightarrow B^\wedge$, with $R,S$ complete regular local power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings, $u$ local and flat, and a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$ whose images extend to one of $S$; in residue characteristic $p>0$ choose $t_1=p$. Put $\overline S=S/\mathfrak m_RS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $\overline S$ is regular local. The surjection $S\to B^\wedge$ induces a surjection $\overline S\to\overline{B^\wedge}:=B^\wedge/\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}B^\wedge$, since $R/\mathfrak m_R\cong A^\wedge/\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=k$ (the horizontal surjection is local).

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), diagram from Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings)

proof.text: *Remove the regular-fibre equations.* The complete closed fibre $\overline{B^\wedge}$ is a Noetherian local quotient of $B^\wedge$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure]. It is formally smooth over $k$ by Step 1 and therefore regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-geometrically-regular] (the trivial field extension gives regularity). The regular local surjection $\overline S\twoheadrightarrow\overline{B^\wedge}$ has kernel generated by elements $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r$ forming part of a regular system of parameters of $\overline S$, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters]. Lift each $\bar x_i$ to $x_i$ in the kernel of $S\twoheadrightarrow B^\wedge$: a lift in $S$ maps to an element of $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}B^\wedge$, hence subtracting a suitable element of $\mathfrak m_RS$ makes it map to zero. In $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2$, the classes of the $t_i$ are independent and the classes of the $x_i$ are independent modulo their span; hence all these classes are independent. Extend them to a basis and use Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] to see that $t_1,\ldots,t_d,x_1,\ldots,x_r$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), paragraph beginning 'As B-bar and S-bar are regular'; Algebra Lemma Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular)

proof.text: Put $T=S/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. The map $S\to B^\wedge$ factors through $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-parameter-quotient] (Stacks 07NM), $T$ is again a complete local power-series ring over the same kind of coefficient field or Cohen ring, with the images of $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ among its parameters (and $t_1=p$ in mixed characteristic). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], these images form a regular sequence, so $R\to T$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular]. Its closed fibre $T/\mathfrak m_RT$ is $\overline S/(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)\cong\overline{B^\wedge}$ as a local $k$-algebra, with the isomorphism induced by $T\to B^\wedge$. It is formally smooth over $k$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology by transport of the lifting property [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), replacement of S by S/(x_1,...,x_r); Lemma Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), Algebra Lemma Tag 07DY (lemma-flat-over-regular)

proof.text: *Identify the completed target with a base change.* The Cohen presentation in Step 2 gives a surjection $R\to A^\wedge$. Let $D=T\otimes_R A^\wedge\cong T/(\ker(R\to A^\wedge))T$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], and let $h:D\to B^\wedge$ be induced by $T\to B^\wedge$ and $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$. It is surjective because $T\to B^\wedge$ is. Both $D$ and $B^\wedge$ are flat over $A^\wedge$: $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] from $R\to T$ flat (Step 4), and $B^\wedge$ by Step 1. Modulo $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}$, $h$ is the isomorphism $T/\mathfrak m_RT\to\overline{B^\wedge}$ of Step 4. If $I=\ker h$, the exact sequence $0\to I\to D\to B^\wedge\to0$ stays left exact after tensoring with $k$, because its last term is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective]; the middle-to-last map is an isomorphism, so $I/\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}I=0$. The ring $D$ is a Noetherian local quotient of $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], so $I$ is finitely generated. Since $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}D$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D$, one has $I/\mathfrak m_D I=0$ as a quotient of $I/\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}I=0$. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with the empty generating family gives $I=0$. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), displayed S tensor_R A -> B and following Nakayama argument; Algebra Lemmas Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) and 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: *It remains to lift for $R\to T$.* If $T$ is formally smooth over $R$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology, [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change] gives the same for $D=T\otimes_R A^\wedge$ over $A^\wedge$ with the extended maximal ideal, which is the maximal ideal of $D$ since $D$ is a local quotient of $T$. Transport through $h:D\cong B^\wedge$ (Step 5) gives formal smoothness of $B^\wedge$ over $A^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. We now prove the needed lifting property for $R\to T$ using its power-series coordinates. To lighten notation write $S=T$, let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $K=S/\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), paragraph after S tensor_R A -> B, invoking Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs)

proof.text: *Reduce a square-zero lifting problem to a residue-vector-space kernel.* Take an $R$-algebra $N$, a square-zero ideal $J\subseteq N$, and an $R$-algebra map $g:S\to N/J$ killing $\mathfrak m^n$ for some $n\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. The map $g$ makes $J$ an $S$-module: $s\cdot j$ is $g(s)j$, independent of a lift of $g(s)$ because $J^2=0$; thus $\mathfrak m^nJ=0$. Set $J_i=\{j\in J: \mathfrak m^i j=0\}$ for $0\le i\le n$. Then $0=J_0\subseteq J_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J_n=J$, and $\mathfrak m(J_{i+1}/J_i)=0$. Each $J_i$ is an ideal of $N$, and each map $N/J_i\to N/J_{i+1}$ has square-zero kernel $J_{i+1}/J_i$. Therefore it suffices to solve the lifting problem for such a kernel, one quotient at a time. In that case $J$ is a $K$-vector space since $S/\mathfrak m=K$ is a field.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph, filtration 0 subset J_1 subset ... subset J_n

proof.text: *An unrestricted lift, then correction of the parameter values.* Assume $\mathfrak mJ=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-fs-adic] (Stacks 07NL), $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ in residue characteristic zero and over $\mathbf Z$ in residue characteristic $p$. The original map $g$ and the map from the prime ring to $N$ form a lifting diagram for this property. In the characteristic-zero case, all nonzero integers are units in $N/J$ because $S$ contains $\mathbf Q$; a unit modulo a square-zero ideal is a unit in $N$ (if $ab=1+j$, inverse $1-j$ corrects it), so $N$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra as required. Hence obtain a ring map $\psi:S\to N$ lifting $g$. The coordinates of $S$ after Step 4 are formal variables $t_1,\ldots,t_d,y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over a coefficient field, or $t_2,\ldots,t_d,y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over a Cohen ring with $t_1=p$. For each $i$, $\psi(t_i)$ and the prescribed image $\varphi(t_i)$ of $R\to N$ differ by an element of $J$. Keep the coefficient-ring map fixed and substitute $\varphi(t_i)$ for $\psi(t_i)$: all variable images are nilpotent because $g(\mathfrak m^n)=0$ and $J^2=0$, so a formal series evaluates through a finite truncation. The resulting map still lifts $g$ and satisfies $\psi(t_i)=\varphi(t_i)$ for every $i$ (automatic for $p$).

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph: lift by Lemma Tag 07NL, then change images of t_i by the universal property of power-series rings

proof.text: *The defect is a derivation from the residue field.* Since $\psi$ lifts $g$ and agrees with $\varphi:R\to N$ on $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, the difference $\Delta=\psi\circ u-\varphi:R\to J$ is additive, satisfies $\Delta(ab)=\varphi(a)\Delta(b)+\varphi(b)\Delta(a)$ (the product of two elements of $J$ is zero), and kills all $t_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], it corresponds to a linear map $\xi: \Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}\to J$. The $R$-action on $J$ factors through $k$ because $u(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak mJ=0$; hence $\xi$ kills $\mathfrak m_R\Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}$. It also kills $\mathrm dt_i$; these generate the image of $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2$ in $k\otimes_R\Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}$ because the $t_i$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$. Exactness of the quotient differential sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] therefore makes $\xi$ factor uniquely through a $k$-linear map $\xi_0:\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to J$. Tensor with $K$ to obtain a $K$-linear map $\xi_K:\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\otimes_kK\to J$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph, derivation D and factorization through Omega_{k/Z}; Algebra Lemma Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega) and Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq)

proof.text: *Extend and subtract the defect.* The closed fibre $\overline S=S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is formally smooth over $k$ (Step 4) and Noetherian local, so [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-differentials-injective] makes $\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\otimes_kK\to\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}\otimes_{\overline S}K$ injective. Extend $\xi_K$ to a $K$-linear map $\xi':\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}\otimes_{\overline S}K\to J$ by extending a basis of the image to a basis of the ambient vector space. Compose $S\to\overline S$, the universal derivation $\mathrm d:\overline S\to\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], reduction to $K$, and $\xi'$ to obtain a derivation $\Delta':S\to J$. For $r\in R$, its value equals $\xi_K(\mathrm d(r\bmod\mathfrak m_R)\otimes1)=\xi_0(\mathrm d(r\bmod\mathfrak m_R))=\Delta(r)$ by Step 9. Thus $\psi'=\psi-\Delta':S\to N$ is a ring homomorphism: additivity and unit are clear, and $\psi'(a)\psi'(b)=\psi(ab)-\psi(a)\Delta'(b)-\psi(b)\Delta'(a)$ since $J^2=0$, equal to $\psi(ab)-\Delta'(ab)$ by Leibniz. Also $\pi\psi'=g$ as $\Delta'$ lands in $J$, and $\psi'\circ u=\varphi$ by the equality of defects. This solves the residue-vector-space case of Step 7; induction along its filtration solves every square-zero lifting problem. Therefore $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for its $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), last paragraph, extension of xi and correction psi'=psi-D'; Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs)

proof.text: *Return from completions.* Steps 6-10 prove that $B^\wedge$ is formally smooth over $A^\wedge$. For an original lifting problem $A\to N$, $J^2=0$, $g:B\to N/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_B^n)=0$, the composite $A\to B\xrightarrow{g}N/J$ kills $\mathfrak m_A^n$ because $f$ is local. Consequently $A\to N$ sends $\mathfrak m_A^n$ into $J$ and kills $\mathfrak m_A^{2n}$; it factors uniquely through $A^\wedge$ using $A/\mathfrak m_A^{2n}\cong A^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2n}$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Similarly $g$ factors through $B/\mathfrak m_B^n\cong B^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge)^n$, giving $g^\wedge:B^\wedge\to N/J$. The two composites $A^\wedge\to N/J$ agree: each kills $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2n}$, each is determined by its restriction to the surjective image of $A$ in $A^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^{2n}$, and those restrictions agree in the original lifting square. Formal smoothness of $B^\wedge/A^\wedge$ supplies a lift $B^\wedge\to N$; restricting it along $B\to B^\wedge$ solves the original diagram. Hence $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.
